docs.title: CubeFit documentation
docs.text:
CubeFit separates a large spectral-fitting problem into four operational layers:

  1. HDF5 preparation — persist observed spectra, templates, LOSVDs, grids, masks, and derived rebinning metadata.
  2. Hypercube generation — convolve each template population with each spatial/component LOSVD and write a chunked (S, C, P, L) basis.
  3. Global NNLS fitting — stream the basis and data, maintain a non-negative (C, P) solution, optionally enforce orbit/component constraints, and checkpoint solver state.
  4. Reconstruction and diagnostics — reconstruct selected spectra or a full model cube, compare residuals, inspect component usage, and validate synthetic runs.

This manual is organized around the current source tree rather than the legacy docs/CubeFit.md. In particular, the active repository contains streaming solver implementations (streaming_nnls.py, streaming_nnls_constrained.py, and streaming_nnls_augmented_rows.py) that supersede the old documentation's detailed Kaczmarz/NNLS-polish narrative.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text: For a new dataset, read HDF5 data model, Hypercube construction, then Workflows. For an existing HDF5 file, begin with Solver and restart model. For failures or numerical surprises, use Troubleshooting.

docs.title: CubeFit — LOSVD-convolved stellar population fitting for IFU cubes
docs.text:
CubeFit builds a hypercube of convolved template spectra for every (spaxel S, component C, population P) and solves for a global, non-negative mixture that best explains the observed IFU data cube. It is designed for large datasets (10^3–10^5 spaxels, 10^2–10^3 populations), is robust to restarts, and uses HDF5 end-to-end with streaming, tile-aligned I/O.

  • Hypercube builder: FFT-based LOSVD convolution on the template grid, followed by flux-conserving rebin to the observed grid.
  • Normalization: choose “model” (LOSVD amplitude) or “data” (per-spaxel observed flux with LOSVD-proportional splits). Convert between modes later without a rebuild.
  • Line emphasis: optional λ-weights so absorption features drive the fit.
  • Solver: multiprocess Kaczmarz with diagonal preconditioning, trust region, backtracking, global step caps, near-zero column freezing, optional de-correlation nudge, and a tile-local weighted NNLS polish.
  • Tracking: streaming fit metrics and optional snapshots to a SWMR-friendly sidecar.
  • Utilities: chunk-aware normalization conversion; global column energy; reconstruction and plotting helpers that never touch the giant /HyperCube/models unless needed.

docs.title: HDF5 layout (what lives where)
docs.text:
Core inputs:

  • /Templates — (P, T) template spectra on the template grid (time domain).
  • /TemPix — (T,) template grid in log-λ (natural log).
  • /ObsPix — (L,) observed wavelength grid (log-λ).
  • /R_T — (T, L) (or (L, T)) flux-conserving linear rebin operator mapping the template grid to the observed grid.
  • /LOSVD — (S, V, C) LOSVD histograms (per spaxel and component).
  • /VelPix — (V,) velocity grid in km/s (for LOSVD).

Optional inputs:

  • /Mask — (L,) boolean wavelength mask; used consistently by builder and solver.
  • /HyperCube/data_flux — (S,) masked mean data flux per spaxel (required for norm="data").

Built artifacts:

  • /HyperCube/models — (S, C, P, L) float32 convolved+rebinned spectra, chunked for streaming and resumable via a _done bitmap.
  • /HyperCube/col_energy — (C, P) float64 global column energy E[c,p] = Σ_{s,λ in mask} A^2, for step-size control.
  • /HyperCube/norm/losvd_amp — (S, C) LOSVD amplitude (sum or trapz).
  • /HyperCube/norm/losvd_amp_sum — (S,) per-spaxel sum of amplitudes.
  • /HyperCube/lambda_weights — (L,) optional λ-weights in [floor, 1] (generated by a median-DoG heuristic).

Fit outputs:

  • /X_global — (C*P,) solution vector, row-major (C, P) flattened.

docs.title: Manager: creating and populating the HDF5 backbone
docs.text:
hdf5_manager.py provides:

  • Safe file open with retries, optional SWMR, and lock-handling (open_h5).
  • Dataset creation for the core arrays and dimensions (H5Manager + H5Dims).
  • Population from NumPy arrays (populate_from_arrays), including grid checks.
  • Flux-conserving rebin operator construction (ensure_rebin_and_resample).

Typical setup:

from CubeFit.hdf5_manager import H5Manager, H5Dims

mgr = H5Manager("galaxy.h5", tem_pix=tem_loglam, obs_pix=obs_loglam)
mgr.init_base(H5Dims(nSpat=S, nLSpec=L, nTSpec=T, nVel=V, nComp=C, nPop=P))
mgr.populate_from_arrays(losvd=H_SVC, datacube=Y_SL, templates=T_PT)
mgr.ensure_rebin_and_resample()  # builds /R_T (and validates shapes)

Notes:

  • /R_T is built by exact bin overlap in log-λ, preserving flux.
  • /Mask (if present) is used later by both builder and solver.
  • Manager helpers centralize chunk-cache setup so downstream is fast.

docs.title: Hypercube builder
docs.text:
hypercube_builder.py constructs /HyperCube/models in streaming, tile-aligned passes:

  1. Kernel from LOSVD: each (s,c) LOSVD row → unit-area kernel on the template grid (linear interpolation to integer pixel shifts). A separate scalar amplitude is computed per (s,c) (either sum or trapezoidal integral).
  2. Convolution (per p): FFT-multiply template by kernel and crop the linear convolution back to the template length.
  3. Rebin to observed grid: multiply by /R_T to get (P, L) for each (s,c).
  4. Normalization:
  5. norm="model": multiply each (s,c,p,:) by its LOSVD amplitude.
  6. norm="data": compute per-spaxel mean observed flux (from /HyperCube/data_flux), then split across components in proportion to their LOSVD amplitudes, preserving the (c) ratios determined by LOSVD at that spaxel.
  7. Global column energy: simultaneously accumulate E[c,p]=Σ_{s,λ in mask} A² into /HyperCube/col_energy for solver preconditioning.

Resumability & chunking: the builder creates /HyperCube/models with chunks (S_chunk, C_chunk, P_chunk, L) and maintains a _done bitmap over the (S_chunk, C_chunk, P_chunk) tile grid; this lets you resume safely or inspect progress mid-build. Metadata is flushed regularly.

docs.title: Normalization conversion (post-hoc)
docs.text:
Flip between norm="data" and norm="model" after the build:

from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import convert_hypercube_norm
convert_hypercube_norm("galaxy.h5", to_mode="model", recompute_energy=True)

This reads /HyperCube/norm/losvd_amp_sum (and /HyperCube/data_flux when needed), computes a per-spaxel scalar F[s], and scales /HyperCube/models[s,:,:,:] *= F[s] in S-tiles (chunk-aligned). It updates /HyperCube/col_energy (optional) and flips the /HyperCube attribute norm.mode. It also respects /Mask when deriving or validating the spaxel flux vector.

This is a safe, no-FFT operation. Use it to avoid rebuilding the hypercube when only a normalization flip is required.

docs.title: λ-feature emphasis (line weights)
docs.text:
Absorption features can be down-weighted in plain least squares. To emphasize them, the solver supports λ-weights:

  • Build weights once via a median spectrum and a two-scale smoothing difference-of-Gaussians (implemented with boxcars), then map to [min_w, 1]. Store at /HyperCube/lambda_weights.
  • During solving, multiply both residuals and design matrix columns by sqrt(w) — equivalent to solving in a diagonal metric where line pixels matter more.

Helpers in cube_utils.py:

from CubeFit.cube_utils import ensure_lambda_weights, read_lambda_weights

w = ensure_lambda_weights("galaxy.h5")  # writes /HyperCube/lambda_weights
w2 = read_lambda_weights("galaxy.h5")   # reads, with floor & mask handling

At solver startup you’ll see a banner printing min/max/mean of the λ-weights used (after masking).

docs.title: Solver: multiprocess batched Kaczmarz (+ weighted NNLS polish)
docs.text:
Entry point:

from CubeFit.pipeline_runner import PipelineRunner

runner = PipelineRunner("galaxy.h5")
x_global, stats = runner.solve_all_mp_batched(
    epochs=E,
    pixels_per_aperture=...,            # row batching (if used)
    lr=...,                             # base learning-rate
    project_nonneg=True,                # x >= 0
    processes=..., blas_threads=...,    # MP and BLAS knobs
    orbit_weights=...,                  # optional (C,) ratio guidance
    # …other optional arguments…
)

High-level flow (pipeline_runner.py → kaczmarz_solver_cchunk_mp.py):

  1. Tile scheduling: sort S-tiles by data norm (coarse “hardest first” ordering).
  2. Workers: each process takes a contiguous c-band for the active S-tile.
  3. Inside a worker (per band):
  4. Sanitize non-finite values in A and R to zeros.
  5. Apply λ-weights by computing gradients and denominators on √w · A and √w · R (but updates and residuals are returned in the unweighted space).
  6. Diagonal preconditioning: per-population step dx_p ∝ g_p / Σ (A_w)^2, blended with global column energy E[c,p] for stability.
  7. Near-zero column freeze (relative & absolute thresholds).
  8. Trust region on ΔR in weighted space (||ΔR_w|| ≤ τ ||R_w||) + backtracking for monotone weighted RMSE drop.
  9. Optional de-correlation nudge to avoid chasing flat null-space directions across P.
  10. Candidate set for tile-local weighted NNLS polish (top-K by score).
  11. Parent process:
  12. Aggregates ΔR over bands and runs tile-level backtracking.
  13. Applies a global step cap using Σ dx² · E[c,p] vs. ||Y||.
  14. Optionally runs NNLS polish on the proposed (c,p) set using a λ-subsample (rows) and accepts only if it reduces weighted RMSE enough.
  15. Commits the single global α for the tile: update R and x, enforce x ≥ 0.
  16. Optional ratio penalty step nudges the component totals toward orbit_weights (if provided).
  17. Streams metrics to FitTracker and snapshots (optional).

The result is written to /X_global (flattened (C*P,)), along with run stats.

docs.title: Reconstruction & plots (without storing a full ModelCube)
docs.text:
You can reconstruct Ŷ = A·x for diagnostics without materializing a full /ModelCube:

  • Reconstruction utilities read A in the same chunk order and contract against x in λ-bands. They write a small target array you name (e.g., /ReconTile) or return the result.
  • Parallel spectral plots pull just the selected rows from /DataCube and the reconstructed array and produce side-by-side data/model spectral plots for worst/best spaxels.

Both are tile-aligned and cache-aware; they never read /HyperCube/models beyond the needed slices.

docs.title: Fit tracking & snapshots
docs.text:
fit_tracker.py provides a non-blocking sidecar writer process:

  • Destination: a sidecar H5 next to the main file (*.fit.<pid>.<ts>.h5).
  • Bounded mp.Queue so the solver never blocks on I/O.
  • SWMR enabled for dashboards.
  • Streams RMSE history, EWMA, progress, and optional x snapshots (best/last/history).

Use tracker=FitTracker(...) in the solver; the runner wires this up for you.

docs.title: Utilities
docs.text:
• Normalization conversion: convert_hypercube_norm(h5, to_mode="model"|"data", recompute_energy=True) — chunk-aligned, mask-aware.
  • Global column energy: created during build; can be recomputed later if you changed normalization.
  • Done-bitmap control: functions to inspect and invalidate _done to resume or redo specific tiles.
  • Recompression: rewrite /HyperCube/models with different compression/filter options (tile-wise copy).

docs.title: Environment variables (knobs)
docs.text: These can be exported to tune performance, stability, or behavior. Defaults shown are what the code uses if you don’t set them.

docs.title: HDF5 & dataset caching
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose HDF5_USE_FILE_LOCKING FALSE Avoid HDF5 file locking issues on shared filesystems. CUBEFIT_RDCC_NSLOTS 400003 File-level raw chunk cache: number of slots. CUBEFIT_RDCC_NBYTES 4294967296 (4 GiB) File-level raw chunk cache size in bytes. CUBEFIT_RDCC_W0 0.9 File-level raw chunk cache preemption policy. CUBEFIT_RDCC_SLOTS 1000003 Per-dataset cache slots used by some readers. CUBEFIT_RDCC_BYTES 268435456 (256 MiB) Per-dataset cache size used by some readers.

docs.title: Multiprocessing & BLAS/OpenMP
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose CUBEFIT_MP_CTX forkserver (fallback spawn) MP start method for the solver pool. OMP_NUM_THREADS set by code BLAS/OpenMP threads per worker (also OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS). KMP_INIT_AT_FORK FALSE Avoid OpenMP deadlocks with fork. SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK (if present) Used by reconstruction helpers to set BLAS threads. PYTHONUNBUFFERED 1 (recommended) Unbuffered stdout for real-time logs on HPC.

docs.title: Solver: worker-level stability & steps (in kaczmarz_solver_cchunk_mp.py)
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose CUBEFIT_BT_STEPS 3 Backtracking steps per band (worker) for monotone weighted RMSE. CUBEFIT_BT_FACTOR 0.5 Multiplicative α shrink in backtracking. CUBEFIT_TRUST_TAU 0.7 Trust-region cap: ||ΔR_w|| ≤ τ ||R_w||. CUBEFIT_EPS 1e-12 Numerical floor in denominators and divisions. CUBEFIT_ZERO_COL_REL 1e-12 Relative threshold (vs median energy) to freeze near-zero columns. CUBEFIT_ZERO_COL_ABS 1e-24 Absolute threshold to freeze columns. CUBEFIT_DEBUG_SAFE 0 Print sanitization/freeze stats per tile if 1. CUBEFIT_NNLS_PROP_PER_BAND 6 How many (c,p) candidates to propose for NNLS polish per band.

docs.title: Solver: aggregation & NNLS polish (in kaczmarz_solver_cchunk_mp.py)
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose CUBEFIT_TILE_BT_STEPS 6 Backtracking steps for the aggregated ΔR across bands. CUBEFIT_TILE_BT_FACTOR 0.5 Aggregated α shrink factor. CUBEFIT_GLOBAL_TAU 0.5 Global step cap using Σ dx²·E[c,p] vs ||Y||. CUBEFIT_GLOBAL_ENERGY_BLEND 1e-3 Blend local Σ(A_w)^2 with global column energy E[c,p] in denominators. CUBEFIT_NNLS_ENABLE 1 Enable tile-local weighted NNLS polish. CUBEFIT_NNLS_EVERY 1 Run NNLS polish every N tiles. CUBEFIT_NNLS_MAX_COLS 128 Max columns K in the NNLS system. CUBEFIT_NNLS_MAX_BYTES 1000000000 Approx memory cap for NNLS system (rows×8 per column). CUBEFIT_NNLS_SUB_L 0 λ-subsample size for NNLS (0 → use all). CUBEFIT_NNLS_SOLVER nnls One of nnls, lsq, mu, fista (FISTA recommended for speed/accuracy). CUBEFIT_NNLS_MAX_ITER 50 Iteration cap for iterative NNLS (mu, fista, lsq’s TRF). CUBEFIT_NNLS_MIN_IMPROVE 0.999 Required weighted-RMSE ratio to accept polish (< this accepts).

docs.title: Solver: λ-weights (in kaczmarz_solver_cchunk_mp.py / cube_utils.py)
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_WEIGHTS_ENABLE 1 Enable λ-weights for solver (√w weighting). CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_WEIGHTS_DSET /HyperCube/lambda_weights Dataset to read. CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_MIN_W 1e-6 Floor on λ-weights; protects √w. CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_WEIGHTS_AUTO 1 Auto-generate weights if missing.

docs.title: Fit tracking (in fit_tracker.py)
docs.text: Variable Default Purpose FITTRACKER_START spawn (or best available) Start method for the tracker process (spawn/forkserver/fork). CUBEFIT_TRACKER_QSIZE 8192 Max queue size; drops messages when full if non-blocking. CUBEFIT_TRACKER_FLUSH_EVERY 128 Flush to disk after this many messages. CUBEFIT_TRACKER_FLUSH_SEC 5.0 Or flush if this many seconds have passed. CUBEFIT_RMSE_STRIDE 16 Only enqueue every Nth batch RMSE sample (sub-sampling).

docs.title: Typical end-to-end workflow
docs.text:
# 1) Build HDF5 backbone & rebin operator
mgr = H5Manager("galaxy.h5", tem_pix=tem_loglam, obs_pix=obs_loglam)
mgr.init_base(H5Dims(nSpat=S, nLSpec=L, nTSpec=T, nVel=V, nComp=C, nPop=P))
mgr.populate_from_arrays(losvd=H_SVC, datacube=Y_SL, templates=T_PT)
mgr.ensure_rebin_and_resample()

# 2) Build hypercube
from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import build_hypercube
build_hypercube("galaxy.h5", norm_mode="data")  # or "model"

# (Optional) Flip normalization later without rebuild
from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import convert_hypercube_norm
convert_hypercube_norm("galaxy.h5", to_mode="model", recompute_energy=True)

# 3) Create λ-weights
from CubeFit.cube_utils import ensure_lambda_weights
ensure_lambda_weights("galaxy.h5")

# 4) Solve
from CubeFit.pipeline_runner import PipelineRunner
runner = PipelineRunner("galaxy.h5")
x, stats = runner.solve_all_mp_batched(
    epochs=6, lr=0.6, project_nonneg=True, processes=8, blas_threads=2,
    orbit_weights=orbit_w  # optional (C,)
)

docs.title: Notes on normalization & physics
docs.text:
• norm="model" keeps each (s,c) model’s scale proportional to the LOSVD amplitude — closest to “physical mass/flux” carried by LOSVD at that spaxel.
  • norm="data" ties the per-spaxel model sum to the observed mean flux (masked), splitting across components in proportion to LOSVD amplitudes. This is convenient for direct data-scale comparisons but can blur absolute differences across datasets. You can switch modes post-hoc with convert_hypercube_norm.

The solver respects /Mask and λ-weights uniformly, so absorption features can dominate the fit when λ-weights are present (verify the printed min/max/mean at startup to ensure they are not all ones).

docs.title: Troubleshooting & sanity checks
docs.text:
• Hypercube completeness: use the _done bitmap helpers to inspect or reset tiles if needed.
  • Normalization flips: use convert_hypercube_norm (streams in S-tiles and handles /Mask); do not read the entire dataset into RAM.
  • Line weights: ensure /HyperCube/lambda_weights exists and spans a range (e.g., min ≪ 1, max ≈ 1); the solver prints min/max/mean.
  • Population mixture looks uniform across components:
  • Confirm λ-weights are applied (banner shows they’re not all 1).
  • Increase epochs modestly; keep GLOBAL_ENERGY_BLEND small but nonzero.
  • Enable NNLS polish with a moderate CUBEFIT_NNLS_MAX_COLS, a λ-subsample (CUBEFIT_NNLS_SUB_L), and CUBEFIT_NNLS_SOLVER=fista for sharper per-tile updates.

docs.title: Where to look in the code
docs.text:
• HDF5 backbone: hdf5_manager.py (safe open, grids, rebin operator).
  • Builder: hypercube_builder.py (FFT conv, normalization, col_energy, chunking + resume).
  • Solver: kaczmarz_solver_cchunk_mp.py (MP loop, λ-weights, trust/backtracking, NNLS polish).
  • Runner: pipeline_runner.py (orchestration, tracking, /X_global).
  • Tracking: fit_tracker.py (sidecar writer, RMSE history, progress, snapshots).
  • Recon/plots: utilities in kz_fitSpec.py (tile-aligned recon) and safe plotting helpers.

docs.text:

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text: CubeFit follows a staged, disk-backed workflow. Observed spectra, LOSVDs, stellar-population templates, and their spectral grids are first assembled in the HDF5 backbone. H5Manager constructs the rebin operator, after which build_hypercube() generates the chunked (S, C, P, L) spectral basis and its support and energy metadata. PipelineRunner then drives the streaming NNLS solve and persists the (C, P) solution in /X_global, while the sidecar tracker provides restart state. Reconstruction, plotting, validation, and diagnostics consume those persisted products without requiring the full design matrix to be materialized in memory.

docs.title: Module responsibilities
docs.text: Module Primary responsibility hdf5_manager.py HDF5 lifecycle, base datasets, grids/rebinning, storage-state management, low-level inspection helpers hypercube_builder.py LOSVD convolution, preflight checks, chunked/resumable basis generation, normalization conversion, column energy hypercube_reader.py Minimal chunk-aware reader for the generated basis streaming_nnls.py Streaming non-negative solver and active-set machinery streaming_nnls_constrained.py Constrained solver variant with explicit regularisation controls streaming_nnls_augmented_rows.py Alternate augmented-row solver implementation pipeline_runner.py User-facing orchestration, warm-start selection, tracker wiring, final solution persistence fit_tracker.py Non-blocking sidecar checkpoint writer and checkpoint loader cube_utils.py Weighting, scaling, component-support, parallelism, solution transforms, diagnostics kz_fitSpec.py Domain workflow, reconstruction, sparse/full spectral diagnostics, post-fit loading plotting.py Fit, white-light, decomposition, and diagnostic JSONL plotting validation.py Synthetic validation-cube creation and solution comparison kz_run.py, kz_rio.py Command-line wrappers for generation/fitting and result loading

docs.title: Design principles visible in the source
docs.text:
The code is structured for datasets too large to treat the full design matrix as a normal in-memory array. HDF5 chunk geometry is therefore part of the computational design, not merely a storage detail. Build and solve stages use spatial tiling, the model basis is persisted once, and reconstruction can operate without materializing all basis columns simultaneously.

Long-running fits are designed to be restartable. PipelineRunner supports zero, saved-solution, and full-resume warm starts; FitTracker writes a sidecar process so checkpoint I/O does not sit directly on the solver's critical path.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: This page lists configuration variables that are present in the supplied source snapshot. Some legacy variables are still set by wrappers even when their effect belongs to alternate/older solver paths; verify the implementation you actually import.

docs.title: Wrapper-configured scientific controls
docs.text: kz_run.py sets a larger family of CUBEFIT_* variables, including lambda/regularisation, orbit-prior, global-energy, and zero-column thresholds. These include CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_AGE, CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_ASMOOTH, CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_FLAT, CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_GROUP, CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_L1, CUBEFIT_LAMBDA_L2, CUBEFIT_ORBIT_BETA, CUBEFIT_ORBIT_PRIOR_WEIGHT, CUBEFIT_GLOBAL_ENERGY_BLEND, CUBEFIT_GLOBAL_TAU, and zero-column controls. Treat these as implementation-specific rather than a stable public configuration API unless the selected solver reads them directly.

docs.title: CPU/thread controls
docs.text: The code uses OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, and MKL_NUM_THREADS to control nested numerical-library parallelism. CLI wrappers inspect SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK. Avoid setting both a high process count and a high BLAS thread count without checking total CPU allocation; oversubscription can reduce throughput substantially.

docs.title: HDF5 data model
docs.text: The HDF5 file is the shared contract between preparation, basis generation, solving, and reconstruction.

docs.title: Core inputs
docs.text:
Dataset Shape Meaning /DataCube (S, L) Observed spectra by spaxel /LOSVD (S, V, C) LOSVD histograms by spaxel and component /Templates (P, T) Stellar-population templates on the template grid /TemPix (T,) Template spectral grid, represented in log wavelength by the current workflow /ObsPix (L,) Observed spectral grid /VelPix (V,) LOSVD velocity grid /Mask (L,) Optional wavelength mask /R_T implementation-defined orientation Linear rebin operator connecting template and observed grids

Dimension metadata may also be stored on the HDF5 root as dims_json and/or dims.* attributes. PipelineRunner falls back to dataset shapes when those attributes are absent.

docs.title: HyperCube products
docs.text: Dataset / attribute Shape Role /HyperCube/models (S, C, P, L) Convolved and rebinned spectral basis /HyperCube/_done tile grid Resume bitmap for basis generation /HyperCube/col_energy (C, P) Global basis-column energy /HyperCube/component_support (n_tiles, C) Spatial-tile/component support inferred from LOSVD amplitudes /HyperCube/norm/losvd_amp (S, C) Per-spaxel/component LOSVD amplitude /HyperCube/norm/losvd_amp_sum (S,) Sum of component amplitudes by spaxel /HyperCube/data_flux (S,) Per-spaxel data scale used by data normalization /HyperCube/lambda_weights (L,) Optional wavelength weights /HyperCube/known_zero_mask (C, P) Persisted solver knowledge that selected coefficients are structurally zero HyperCube.attrs['norm.mode'] scalar Current basis normalization mode HyperCube.attrs['complete'] scalar Whether the basis build is complete

docs.title: Fit output
docs.text: The current PipelineRunner writes /X_global as a two-dimensional (C, P) float64 dataset, with attributes layout='C_P' and P=<population count>. This differs from older documentation that described a flattened (C*P,) dataset. Helper functions may still accept flattened vectors at API boundaries, so callers should inspect the specific function contract rather than assuming one representation everywhere.

docs.title: Storage-state utilities
docs.text: hdf5_manager.py includes utilities to classify, archive, restore, compact, and inspect /HyperCube/models. These are operationally important for large files: archiving/repacking changes storage characteristics, while solver-ready restoration must preserve the expected logical dataset geometry.

docs.title: Preflight first
docs.text: Before a large build, use preflight_hypercube_convolution() or assert_preflight_ok(). The preflight compares the convolution path on a small subset and checks response/shift tolerances before expensive generation begins. A separate estimate_global_velocity_bias_prebuild() helper can estimate a single velocity offset before the build.

docs.title: Builder API
docs.text:
from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import build_hypercube

build_hypercube(
    "galaxy.h5",
    norm_mode="model",       # or "data"
    amp_mode="sum",          # or supported alternative such as "trapz"
    cp_flux_ref_mode="median",
    S_chunk=128,
    C_chunk=1,
    P_chunk=360,
    compression=None,
    vel_bias_kms=0.0,
    processes=None,
    blas_threads=None,
)

The builder reads templates, LOSVDs, spectral grids, mask information, and the rebin operator; constructs LOSVD kernels; performs template convolution; rebins to the observed grid; applies the selected normalization; and writes /HyperCube/models in chunk-aligned tiles.

docs.title: Normalization modes
docs.text:
model normalization preserves the LOSVD-amplitude scaling of each component. data normalization uses /HyperCube/data_flux to place the model on a per-spaxel data scale while retaining component ratios derived from LOSVD amplitudes.

Normalization can be changed after generation with:

from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import convert_hypercube_norm

convert_hypercube_norm(
    "galaxy.h5",
    to_mode="model",
    recompute_energy=True,
)

This is an in-place streaming conversion and can avoid a full convolution rebuild.

docs.title: Resumability and support metadata
docs.text: The build maintains /HyperCube/_done, allowing completed tiles to be skipped after interruption. It also creates /HyperCube/component_support, marking whether each component has non-negligible LOSVD amplitude within each spatial tile. Column-energy metadata can be generated or regenerated with ensure_global_column_energy().

docs.title: Parallelism
docs.text: Generation accepts process and BLAS-thread controls directly. The source also recognizes CUBEFIT_GEN_PROCESSES and CUBEFIT_GEN_BLAS_THREADS, with BLAS/OpenMP thread variables propagated for worker control.

docs.title: Current solver family
docs.text:
The repository contains three streaming solver modules. streaming_nnls.py is imported by pipeline_runner.py in the supplied snapshot. streaming_nnls_constrained.py contains a closely related constrained implementation with explicit scientific regularisation controls, while streaming_nnls_augmented_rows.py is another solver variant.

The old manual's detailed description of a multiprocess Kaczmarz solver with tile-local NNLS polish is therefore no longer an accurate description of the current primary call path.

docs.title: Public orchestration API
docs.text:
from CubeFit.pipeline_runner import PipelineRunner

runner = PipelineRunner("galaxy.h5")
x_cp, stats = runner.solve_all_mp_batched(
    reader_s_tile=128,
    reader_c_tile=1,
    reader_p_tile=360,
    reader_dtype_models="float32",
    reader_apply_mask=True,
    processes=8,
    blas_threads=2,
    orbit_weights=None,
    x0=None,
    warm_start="zeros",       # "zeros", "saved_x", or "resume"
    regularisation_scale=1.0,
    tracker_mode="on",
)

See the signature-mismatch warning in Troubleshooting for this exact repository snapshot.

docs.title: Warm starts
docs.text:
warm_start="zeros" initializes a fresh zero solution. warm_start="saved_x" searches the latest tracker sidecar and the main HDF5 file and selects a valid saved solution. warm_start="resume" attempts to restore both coefficients and matching solver state from the newest checkpoint; if a complete checkpoint is unavailable, the runner can fall back to a saved coefficient vector.

An explicit x0 takes precedence over these modes and is validated for expected length and finite values.

docs.title: Checkpointing
docs.text:
FitTracker runs a separate writer process. The active interface is intentionally small: the solver can queue save_checkpoint(x, state) messages, and load_checkpoint() restores the latest coefficient vector plus resumable state. NullTracker provides the same interface when tracking is disabled.

CUBEFIT_SOLVER_CHECKPOINT_EVERY controls solver checkpoint cadence in the streaming solver code. Tracker queue capacity is controlled by CUBEFIT_TRACKER_QSIZE.

docs.title: Diagnostics
docs.text: The streaming solver can emit JSONL diagnostics controlled by CUBEFIT_DIAG_LEVEL, CUBEFIT_DIAG_STRIDE, CUBEFIT_DIAG_TOPK, and CUBEFIT_DIAG_JSONL. plot_diagnostic_jsonl_dashboard() in plotting.py consumes diagnostic JSONL files.

docs.title: Orbit/component constraints
docs.text: The solver accepts optional orbit_weights. Utility functions in cube_utils.py provide component-weight comparison, soft-box/projection operations, component support construction, and upscaling/constraining helpers. The constrained solver variant includes explicit orbit-mass correction and scientific regularisation machinery.

docs.title: Runner / streaming-solver signature mismatch
docs.text:
In the supplied snapshot, PipelineRunner.solve_all_mp_batched() calls:

solve_streaming_nnls(
    ...,
    regularisation_scale=regularisation_scale,
)

but streaming_nnls.py::solve_streaming_nnls() does not declare a regularisation_scale keyword. Calling this exact path will therefore raise a TypeError unless the runtime module differs from the packed source or the mismatch is patched. streaming_nnls_constrained.py contains a solver variant whose solve_streaming_nnls() does accept regularisation_scale, suggesting an incomplete integration between solver variants.

Before production runs, make the import/call contract consistent and add a smoke test that instantiates PipelineRunner and executes a tiny solve.

docs.title: Documentation/source drift
docs.text: The old docs/CubeFit.md describes a Kaczmarz solver with trust regions, backtracking, and tile-local weighted NNLS polish. The current primary runner imports a streaming NNLS implementation instead. Do not use the old solver tuning tables as authoritative for the current solver without verifying the variable is read by the selected implementation.

docs.title: /X_global shape drift
docs.text: Older documentation describes /X_global as flattened (C*P,). The current runner writes the solver result as (C, P) and stamps layout='C_P'. Some helper functions still flatten inputs internally. When interoperating with older files, inspect dataset dimensionality and reshape explicitly using known (C, P) metadata.

docs.title: Environment specification drift
docs.text: README.md names dependencies such as SciPy, h5py, threadpoolctl, and optional Cython, while environment.yml in the snapshot lists only Python, NumPy, Matplotlib, Zarr, numcodecs, and tqdm. The environment file therefore does not appear sufficient to reproduce all imports exercised by the current codebase. Consolidate dependencies into one authoritative environment specification.

docs.title: MkDocs navigation
docs.text: The existing mkdocs.yml references docs/index.md, but the packed directory listing contains only docs/CubeFit.md, docs/CubeFit.html, and docs/CubeFit.pdf. This overhaul supplies docs/index.md and a complete multi-page navigation replacement.

docs.title: HyperCube incomplete
docs.text: Use print_hypercube_done_status() to inspect the _done bitmap. If a tile must be regenerated deliberately, use invalidate_done() rather than deleting arbitrary HDF5 slices. Confirm HyperCube.attrs['complete'] before fitting.

docs.title: Model/data wavelength mismatch
docs.text: The streaming solver explicitly checks that /HyperCube/models.shape[-1] matches /DataCube.shape[1]. Rebuild or correct the rebinning/grid setup rather than bypassing this check.

docs.title: Multiprocessing is slower than expected
docs.text: Check process count × BLAS threads against allocated CPUs. On SLURM, compare settings with SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK. Use resolve_parallelism() or recommend_streaming_architecture() as starting points, and avoid nested oversubscription.

docs.title: 1. Prepare an HDF5 file
docs.text: For programmatic setup, use H5Manager or populate_base_from_arrays() to persist LOSVDs, the observed data cube, templates, optional mask, and spectral grids. Use set_spectral_grids()/manager helpers to persist grids and build the rebinning artifacts required by the HyperCube builder.

docs.title: 2. Validate the convolution path
docs.text:
from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import assert_preflight_ok

assert_preflight_ok("galaxy.h5")

For datasets with a suspected global velocity offset, estimate it before generation with estimate_global_velocity_bias_prebuild() and pass the resulting value as vel_bias_kms to build_hypercube().

docs.title: 3. Build or resume the HyperCube
docs.text:
from CubeFit.hypercube_builder import build_hypercube

build_hypercube(
    "galaxy.h5",
    norm_mode="model",
    amp_mode="sum",
    S_chunk=128,
    C_chunk=1,
    P_chunk=360,
)

The _done bitmap makes repeated calls resumable. print_hypercube_done_status() and invalidate_done() in hdf5_manager.py support inspection and deliberate rebuilds.

docs.title: 4. Fit
docs.text: Instantiate PipelineRunner only after the base datasets exist. Choose a warm-start mode deliberately: zeros for a new fit, saved_x to reuse only coefficients, or resume to restore solver state when possible.

docs.title: 5. Reconstruct
docs.text: For a full stored model cube, use reconstruct_modelcube_fast() or reconstruct_modelcube_fast_parallel() from kz_fitSpec.py. For selected spaxels, reconstruct_model_spectrum() in hdf5_manager.py or plot_sparse_spectra_from_x() avoids generating a full /ModelCube.

docs.title: 6. Diagnose
docs.text: Use plot_aperture_fit() for observed/model spectra, plot_white_light_images() for spatial summaries, plot_model_decomposition() for decomposition views, and plot_diagnostic_jsonl_dashboard() for solver JSONL diagnostics. compare_orbit_vs_solution_absolute() examines component/orbit constraint behavior.

docs.title: 7. Validate with synthetic data
docs.text: validation.py can create a minimal validation cube from an existing model cube and compare the recovered solution with the generating solution. This is the preferred path for checking end-to-end recovery after solver or normalization changes.

docs.title: CLI wrappers
docs.text: kz_run.py wraps genCubeFit() for generation/fitting and accepts --galaxy, --run-switch, --ncomp, and redraw flags. kz_rio.py wraps loadCubeFit() for result loading/analysis. Both infer CPU availability from SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK when present, with repository-specific fallbacks.
